title: Swipe a magnetic-stripe card through a desktop reader in one pass
instruction: Pick up the card, swipe it through the reader once, then stand it in the card stand.
context: Most payment cards now tap or use the chip, yet magnetic stripes are still swiped every working day: gift and prepaid cards at the till, payment cards when the chip fails, hotel key cards at the front desk, badges at time clocks. A swipe reads only if the stripe faces the head, the card rides the slot floor so its track crosses the head gap, and the whole stripe passes in one stroke inside the reader's rated speed. Done by: cashiers (O*NET 41-2011.00; https://www.onetonline.org/link/summary/41-2011.00) and hotel desk clerks (O*NET 43-4081.00; https://www.onetonline.org/link/summary/43-4081.00).
setup: Station tabletop (the counter) z=0.7475 m, spanning x -0.19 to 0.91 m, y -0.65 to 0.65 m; x forward, y left; arm bases (0,+/-0.305,0.75) m. Metres. Card reader: MagTek Dynamag MagneSafe swipe reader, part 21073075 (USB HID), black ABS plastic, fixed to the counter with fastening tape as its manual allows; origin (0.316,-0.30723,0.7475), yaw -90 deg, so its slot runs along world x on the line y=-0.305 straight out from the right arm's base and the head side faces +y. Reader frame (x across the slot, y along it): body 0.0316 (x) by 0.0995 (y) by 0.0304 (z); the slot runs along y between x -0.00276 and -0.0017 (1.06 mm wide, inside the maker's 0.864-1.067 mm), floor 0.00776 above the counter (22.6 mm deep), 0.8 mm rounding on its top edges; straight for |y|<=0.03475, then four fixed 2 mm black plastic mouth walls flare it to 5.06 mm wide at both ends (y +/-0.04975). Read head: steel cylinder radius 0.0045, height 0.0123 (0.01236 to 0.02466 above the counter), axis at reader (-0.0062,0), in a window of the front (head-side) wall; it slides along x on a 1700 N/m spring preloaded 0.1 mm, travel 0 to -0.0015, damping 2 N s/m, 3 g; at rest its face is level with the slot's back wall (zero gap), and its gap is 0.0104 above the slot floor (track 2's centreline). A 0.2 mm silver strip on the top front marks the head side; status LED radius 0.0028 on the top at reader (0.0080,0.0312): green when ready, red for 2 s after a failed swipe. Card stand: fixed grey ABS plastic desk stand, yaw 0, origin (0.235,-0.410,0.7475): base 0.024 by 0.108 by 0.004; a 1.6 mm slot 100 mm long along y with walls up to 0.015, then 3 mm radius rounded lips opening to 7.6 mm at the 0.018 top. Card: ISO/IEC 7810 ID-1 card, rigid PVC plastic box 0.0856 by 0.05398 by 0.00076, 0.0049 kg, square corners, dynamic; lying flat on the counter just in front of the stand, centre (0.165,-0.405,0.7479), long side along y, its -y end 202 mm from the counter's right edge (y=-0.65). Its black magnetic stripe (visual band 5.54 to 15.95 mm from one long edge, ISO/IEC 7811 three-track area) is on the upper face, along the +x long edge (away from the robot); the blue printed front faces down onto the counter. The stand starts empty. Friction static/dynamic (estimates, not measured): card 0.40/0.35, stand 0.40/0.35, reader body and mouths 0.30/0.25, head 0.20/0.15; contact offsets card and stand 0.5 mm, reader 1.5 mm; restitution zero. The card is never jittered at reset.
scoring: From the card's pose and velocity and the head's push-back, sampled at 20 Hz. Contact: the head pushed back at least 0.38 mm. A swipe is a run of contact samples plus the sample before and after; swipes that never bring the head between 6.94 and 78.67 mm from a card end (the encoded data, ISO/IEC 7811-4) are ignored. A swipe is a good read when the samples are consecutive; the head crosses that whole span in one direction (no reversal over 0.1 mm while on the span); card speed at the head is 0.1524 to 1.524 m/s (the reader's rated 6 to 60 in/s) at every sample on the span, as the average between every pair of consecutive samples that are both on the span, and as the average between consecutive samples on opposite sides of the whole span (motion past the span's ends is not checked); and while the data passes the head the stripe faces the head (within 60 degrees), the stripe edge is down (within 60 degrees), and the stripe edge at the head is 2.0 mm below to 1.0 mm above the slot floor (a real head pivots to follow tilt, so tilt counts only through this height). These three are checked at every sample on the span (the untouched samples just before and after the touched run included) and, where two consecutive samples cross the 6.94 mm or 78.67 mm end of the span, at that end, interpolated linearly between the two samples (so a card lifted out of, or dropped into, the slot over the head while data passes it fails, and a card that leaves the floor only beyond the span does not). A swipe whose head contact has not ended by the end of the run is judged on its samples so far (no sample after it needed) if the head has already crossed the whole 6.94 to 78.67 mm span; otherwise it is a failed swipe: alone it gives no read (0); after a good swipe it makes the read late. Clean read: exactly one swipe and it is good. Late read: a good swipe among two or more (a good read after a failed swipe, or a second swipe after a good one). In the stand: both ends of the card's bottom edge inside the 1.6 by 100 mm slot (0.5 mm tolerance) and within 2 mm of the slot floor, long axis within 10 degrees of the slot, plane within 15 degrees of vertical, either face forward. Done: in the stand, both gripper TCPs at least 30 mm from the card's bounding box, card below 0.01 m/s and 0.5 rad/s, for 1 s. Score at the end of the run: 0 with no good read, or if the card ever fell off the counter (let go, both gripper TCPs at least 30 mm from its bounding box, with its centre more than 20 mm below the counter's surface); a card lying on the counter or held past its edge is not dropped; clean read 1.0 when done, else 0.5; late read 0.5 when done, else 0.25. The LED is never scored. The reader is fixed, so it cannot be knocked.
reset_notes: Lay the card flat on the counter at its marked spot, stripe face up along the long edge away from the robot, printed front down; the stand empty; the head returns to its stop. Nothing is consumed. Real trials: a test card with track 2 encoded, the reader fixed with its fastening tape, and the host's last read cleared; its own LED and decoded data confirm each read.
fidelity: Rigid 0.76 mm PVC card (a real one flexes, which can help lift its edge; bending is not modelled) in a 1.06 mm slot at 240 Hz, 32 solver iterations. The head is a steel cylinder on a sprung slide. Magnetic decoding is not simulated: the scorer applies the reader's documented conditions (stripe face, edge height at the head, one pass, 6 to 60 in/s) to the simulated card. Friction is estimated. The reader is fixed (tape). The LED, driven by the same physical state, does not go dark mid-swipe.
